sections.content: How many people stayed in Southampton after gaining qualifications?

Southampton is a city in the South East. Southampton also has a university.

Southampton has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Southampton ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 9,820 state-school pupils from Southampton who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,260 (23%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 3,015 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Southampton to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Southampton's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Southampton in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Southampton move to?

Of Southampton's graduates, 710 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 145 of those graduates (20%) were living fairly locally, in the Southampton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Southampton's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 555 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 240 of those qualified non-graduates (43%) were living fairly locally, in the Southampton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Southampton's GCSE cohort:

  • 450 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 245 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was the South West

In 2018 to 2019, 61% of graduates and 34% of qualified non-graduates living in Southampton had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 3,885 graduates and 3,625 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Southampton. This is compared with the 2,260 graduates and 3,015 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 39% of the graduates had also lived in Southampton as GCSE pupils, while 61% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Southampton in 2018 to 2019, 66% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 34% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
